Name: No meaningful category applies
Explanation: Statements not covered by any other category. Use restrictively. Statements opposing agricultural policy are coded 000.
Notes: Statements opposing agricultural policy are coded 000

Name: Foreign Special Relationships: Positive
Explanation: Favourable mentions of particular countries with which the manifesto country has a special relationship; the need for co-operation with and/or aid to such countries.

Name: Foreign Special Relationships: Negative
Explanation: Negative mentions of particular countries with which the manifesto country has a special relationship.

Name: Anti-Imperialism: Positive
Explanation: Negative references to imperial behaviour and/or negative references to one state exerting strong influence (political, military or commercial) over other states.

Name: Military: Positive
Explanation: The importance of external security and defence.
Tricky_Example: A capable military ensures we can maintain peace through strong deterrence.
Counter_Example_1: Conflicts should be resolved through diplomacy and international mediation.

Name: Military: Negative
Explanation: Negative references to the military or use of military power to solve conflicts.

Name: Peace: Positive
Explanation: Any declaration of belief in peace and peaceful means of solving crises -- absent  reference to the military.
Tricky_Example: Peaceful resolution of conflicts requires patient engagement even with adversaries.
Counter_Example_1: International disputes require patient diplomacy and negotiation rather than military force.

Name: Internationalism: Positive
Explanation: Need for international co-operation, including co-operation with specific countries  other than those coded in 101 or 108.

Name: European Integration: Positive
Explanation: Favourable mentions of European Community/Union in general.

Name: Internationalism: Negative
Explanation: Negative references to international co-operation.

Name: European Integration: Negative
Explanation: Negative references to the European Community/Union.

Name: Freedom and Human Rights: Positive
Explanation: Favourable mentions of importance of personal freedom and civil rights in the  manifesto and other countries.
Tricky_Example: Protection from government surveillance and corporate data collection protects personal liberty.
Counter_Example_1: To prevent crimes, private spaces must also be monitored.

Name: Democracy: Positive
Explanation: Favourable mentions of democracy as the "only game in town".
Tricky_Example: Think globally - act locally: Global justice cannot be achieved without the participation of citizens and civil society.
Counter_Example_1: In addition, we want to enshrine net neutrality in law.

Name: Constitutionalism: Positive
Explanation: Support for maintaining the status quo of the constitution.

Name: Constitutionalism: Negative
Explanation: Opposition to the entirety or specific aspects of the manifesto country's constitution.

Name: Decentralisation: Positive
Explanation: Support for federalism or decentralisation of political and/or economic power.

Name: Centralisation: Positive
Explanation: General opposition to political decision-making at lower political levels.

Name: Governmental and Administrative Efficiency: Positive
Explanation: Government efficiency, reducing bureaucracy, digital administration.
Notes: Specific policy positions overrule this category! If there is no specific policy position, however, this category applies.

Name: Political Corruption: Negative
Explanation: Need to eliminate political corruption and associated abuses of political and/or  bureaucratic power.

Name: Political Authority: Positive
Explanation: References to the manifesto party's competence to govern and/or other party's lack of such competence.
Notes: Specific policy positions overrule this category! If there is no specific policy position, however, this category applies.

Name: Free Enterprise: Positive
Explanation: Favourable mentions of the free market and free market capitalism as an economic  model.

Name: Incentives: Positive
Explanation: Supply-side economic policies, incentives and assistance to businesses.
Tricky_Example: Targeted tax relief to boost our start-up scene.

Name: Market Regulation: Positive
Explanation: Fair open market, anti-monopoly, consumer protection, market rules.
Notes: Focus on rules of the market. Not general economic growth (410).
Tricky_Example: that is, each mineral water should be drunk according to the pathology it is intended to treat; however, the Ministry has not carried out research on the matter.
Counter_Example_1: From now on, there will be 4 compulsory subjects in the final exam.

Name: Economic Planning: Positive
Explanation: Favourable mentions of long-standing economic planning by the government.

Name: Corporatism: Positive
Explanation: Favourable mentions of cooperation of government, employers, and trade unions  simultaneously.

Name: Protectionism: Positive
Explanation: Favourable mentions of extending or maintaining the protection of internal markets  (by the manifesto or other countries).

Name: Protectionism: Negative
Explanation: Support for the concept of free trade and open markets. Call for abolishing all means of  market protection (in the manifesto or any other country).

Name: Economic Goals
Explanation: Broad economic goals, such as prosperity, that are not tied to a specific policy instrument or another category.
Notes: Specific policy positions overrule this category! If there is no specific policy position, however, this category applies.

Name: Keynesian Demand Management: Positive
Explanation: Favourable mentions of demand side oriented economic policies (assistance to consumers rather than businesses).

Name: Economic Growth: Positive
Explanation: Support for classic economic growth and production.
Notes: If growth is criticized or replaced by sustainability goals, use 416.

Name: Technology and Infrastructure: Positive
Explanation: Modernisation of infrastructure (transport, broadband) and technology/research.
Notes: Infrastructure/Research only. Digital administration -> 303. Business incentives -> 402.

Name: Controlled Economy: Positive
Explanation: Support for direct government control of economy. May include, for instance:  - Control over prices;  - Introduction of minimum wages.

Name: Nationalisation: Positive
Explanation: Favourable mentions of government ownership of industries, either partial or complete.

Name: Economic Orthodoxy: Positive
Explanation: Need for economically healthy government policy making.

Name: Marxist Analysis: Positive
Explanation: Positive references to Marxist-Leninist ideology and specific use of Marxist-Leninist  terminology by the manifesto party (typically but not necessary by communist parties).

Name: Anti-Growth Economy: Positive
Explanation: Rejection of the growth paradigm. Call for sustainable economic development.
Notes: Vs 501: 416 focuses on transforming the economy/growth. Vs 410: 416 limits classic growth.
Tricky_Example: We need an economy that respects planetary boundaries.

Name: Environmental Protection: Positive
Explanation: Preservation of nature, climate protection, and environment.
Notes: Pure nature protection. For systemic economic transformation or growth critique, use 416.
Counter_Example_1: Noise abatement programs and technical innovations like whisper asphalt contribute to this. [NOT environmental protection - this is TECHNOLOGY/INFRASTRUCTURE]

Name: Culture: Positive
Explanation: Need for state funding of cultural and leisure facilities including arts and sport.

Name: Equality: Positive
Explanation: Social justice, fair treatment, anti-discrimination, equality.
Notes: Focus on rights/justice. Concrete increases in welfare/pensions -> 504.
Tricky_Example: Equal pay for equal work for men and women.

Name: Welfare State Expansion
Explanation: Favourable mentions of need to introduce, maintain or expand any public social service  or social security scheme.
Tricky_Example: The fight for health in the workplace will be declared a national cause in the first year of our mandate.
Counter_Example_1: From now on, there will be 4 compulsory subjects in the final exam.

Name: Welfare State Limitation
Explanation: Limiting state expenditures on social services or social security.

Name: Education Expansion
Explanation: Need to expand and/or improve educational provision at all levels.
Notes: This excludes technical training which is coded under 411.

Name: Education Limitation
Explanation: Limiting state expenditure on education.

Name: National Way of Life: Positive
Explanation: Favourable mentions of the manifesto country's nation, history, and general appeals.
Tricky_Example: The diversity of educational paths is our strength.
Counter_Example_1: In addition, we want to enshrine net neutrality in law.

Name: National Way of Life: Negative
Explanation: Unfavourable mentions of the manifesto country's nation and history.
Tricky_Example: Excessive nationalism and national pride hinder global cooperation and understanding.
Counter_Example_1: Our national heritage is deeply valued and should be celebrated.

Name: Traditional Morality: Positive
Explanation: Favourable mentions of traditional and/or religious moral values.
Tricky_Example: Religious institutions provide essential moral values and community that society needs.
Counter_Example_1: Religious institutions have historically opposed progress in civil rights and scientific advancement.

Name: Traditional Morality: Negative
Explanation: Opposition to traditional and/or religious moral values.
Tricky_Example: Separation of church and state and diverse family forms must be legally protected.
Counter_Example_1: Family stability and shared moral values are essential foundations for social cohesion.

Name: Law and Order: Positive
Explanation: Strict law enforcement, police, domestic crime prevention.
Tricky_Example: More police presence on our streets.

Name: Civic Mindedness: Positive
Explanation: Appeals for national solidarity and the need for society to see itself as united.

Name: Multiculturalism: Positive
Explanation: Favourable mentions of cultural diversity and cultural plurality within domestic  societies.

Name: Multiculturalism: Negative
Explanation: The enforcement or encouragement of cultural integration. Appeals for cultural  homogeneity in society.
Tricky_Example: As the main lever of republican integration, it is also the main place where a demanding conception of citizenship is promoted.
Counter_Example_1: Immigrants must learn our language and adopt our national cultural values.

Name: Labour Groups: Positive
Explanation: Favourable references to all labour groups, the working class, and unemployed workers  in general.
Notes: Specific policy positions overrule all 7th domain (except 703)! If there is no specific policy position, however, these categories apply.

Name: Labour Groups: Negative
Explanation: Negative references to labour groups and trade unions. May focus specifically on the  danger of unions "abusing power".

Name: Agriculture and Farmers: Positive
Explanation: Specific policies in favour of agriculture and farmers.
Notes: Statements opposing agricultural policy are coded 000

Name: Middle Class and Professional Groups: Positive
Explanation: General favourable references to the middle class.
Notes: This is not an economical category but refers to the social group(s).

Name: Underprivileged Minority Groups
Explanation: Very general favourable references to underprivileged minorities who are defined  neither in economic nor in demographic terms (e.
Notes: Only includes favourable statements that cannot be classified in other  categories (e.g. 503, 504, 604 etc.)

Name: Non-Economic Demographic Groups: Positive
Explanation: General favourable mentions of demographically defined special interest groups of all  kinds.
Notes: Might include references to assistance to these groups, but only if these do not fall under other categories (e.g. 503 or 504).
